findings.highlight: Touma Kazusa confirmed to settle down in Japan.
findings.evidenceJa: スポーツ紙や大衆週刊誌はこぞって『冬馬かずさ　今後は日本を拠点に活動』と報道し、誤解はとうとう世間にまで浸透した。
findings.explanation: The mistaken reports say Kazusa will henceforth base her professional activities in Japan. The English upgrades that to a confirmed permanent personal settlement, conflating the media's inference with Youko's separate permanent-residence announcement.
findings.japanese:
スポーツ紙や大衆週刊誌はこぞって
『冬馬かずさ　今後は日本を拠点に活動』と報道し、
誤解はとうとう世間にまで浸透した。
findings.todokanai: From sports weeklys to gossip magazines, it was reported as "Touma Kazusa confirmed to settle down in Japan." And this misunderstanding has already spread to the general public.

findings.highlight: Kazusa's popularity in Japan experienced another boom
findings.evidenceJa: その流れは、コンサートのブルーレイ発売発表と絡み、日本に、新たな冬馬家ブームを巻き起こした。
findings.explanation: The announcement and Blu-ray news create a new boom around the Touma family as a public phenomenon—mother and daughter together. The English narrows this to another rise in Kazusa's individual popularity.
findings.japanese:
その流れは、コンサートのブルーレイ発売発表と絡み、
日本に、新たな冬馬家ブームを巻き起こした。
findings.todokanai: And thanks to that, Kazusa's popularity in Japan experienced another boom, with blu-ray recordings of her concert being announced.

findings.highlight: By being with me, she'll be happy. She'll smile for me just by being next to me…
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつが俺の側にいることで幸せになってくれるなら。隣にいるときだけでも笑ってくれるなら…」
findings.explanation: Haruki offers a conditional justification: if being beside him makes Kazusa happy, if she can smile at least while she is beside him. The English turns that fragile hope into confident statements that she will be happy and smile for him.
findings.japanese:
「あいつが俺の側にいることで
幸せになってくれるなら。
隣にいるときだけでも笑ってくれるなら…」
findings.todokanai: "By being with me, she'll be happy. She'll smile for me just by being next to me…"

findings.highlight: "Well, I do plan on living moderately long."
findings.evidenceJa: 「ま、ほどほどに生きるつもり」
findings.explanation: ほどほどに生きる means Youko plans to live with moderation; 'living moderately long' converts manner into lifespan — Kazusa's pleas for treatment compliance and Youko's promise to keep living remain.
findings.japanese: 「ま、ほどほどに生きるつもり」
findings.todokanai: "Well, I do plan on living moderately long."

findings.highlight: "You left the Vienna office to me. I won't be able to do anything useful for it, but Haruki will be able to do anything."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ウィーンの事務所の方は任せといて。
あたしは役に立たないけど、
春希が何もかもやってくれるから」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says to leave the Vienna office to her; the English changes this into a past action by Youko — Haruki's future operational role and Kazusa's self-deprecation remain explicit.
findings.japanese:
「ウィーンの事務所の方は任せといて。
あたしは役に立たないけど、
春希が何もかもやってくれるから」
findings.todokanai: "You left the Vienna office to me. I won't be able to do anything useful for it, but Haruki will be able to do anything."

findings.highlight: If you're going to play, make sure you enjoy it… and make him happy.
findings.evidenceJa: 「贖罪のための演奏なんてつまんない。やるならとことん色っぽく楽しみなさい。…そうやって彼を幸せにしてあげなさい」
findings.explanation: Youko tells Kazusa not merely to enjoy playing, but to enjoy it thoroughly and sensually/sexily, and thereby make Haruki happy. Dropping 色っぽく erases the route-long identification of Kazusa's erotic feeling with the mature color of her piano.
findings.japanese:
「贖罪のための演奏なんてつまんない。
やるならとことん色っぽく楽しみなさい。
…そうやって彼を幸せにしてあげなさい」
findings.todokanai: "No one wants to hear a musical performance born from a desire for atonement. If you're going to play, make sure you enjoy it… and make him happy."

findings.highlight: it was the only thing I wanted to keep, only so I could give it back to the manufacturer.
findings.evidenceJa: 荷物を運び出し、鍵を返したとき、それだけは捨てるつもりで手に持っていたのを、業者に渡し忘れていただけ。
findings.explanation: Haruki had the guitar in his hand intending to throw it away and simply forgot to hand it to the removal contractor. The English reverses disposal into wanting to keep it and misreads the contractor as the guitar's manufacturer.
findings.japanese:
荷物を運び出し、鍵を返したとき、
それだけは捨てるつもりで手に持っていたのを、
業者に渡し忘れていただけ。
findings.todokanai: When I had carried out all my luggage and handed over the key, it was the only thing I wanted to keep, only so I could give it back to the manufacturer.

findings.highlight: I also trust they'll handle it appropriately.
findings.evidenceJa: 多分今ごろは管理会社が見つけて、ちょっと迷惑そうな態度で、適当に処分してるはず。
findings.explanation: Haruki imagines the management company finding the abandoned guitar and disposing of it casually, with some annoyance. The English instead says he trusts them to handle it appropriately, reversing the contemptuous finality of the image.
findings.japanese:
多分今ごろは管理会社が見つけて、
ちょっと迷惑そうな態度で、適当に処分してるはず。
findings.todokanai: I imagine the management company is handling it with a rather troubled attitude, though I also trust they'll handle it appropriately.

findings.highlight: I feel something running down my cheeks.
findings.evidenceJa: かずさの優しい声と温かい息が耳にかかり、そして、目元に柔らかい布が押しつけられる。
findings.explanation: Kazusa leans close and presses a soft cloth to Haruki's eyes, gently wiping tears he has not noticed. The English replaces her consoling physical action with liquid running down his cheeks.
findings.japanese:
かずさの優しい声と温かい息が耳にかかり、
そして、目元に柔らかい布が押しつけられる。
findings.todokanai: The sensation of Kazusa's warm, gentle breath touches my ears, and I feel something running down my cheeks.

findings.highlight: She wants to hold me tight, but she can't bring herself to…
findings.evidenceJa: 抱きしめたいけれど、抱きしめられない…
findings.explanation: Kazusa wants to embrace Haruki but physically cannot because both are strapped into airplane seats; she reaches as far as she can. 'Can't bring herself to' instead attributes emotional hesitation to her at the moment of wholehearted consolation.
findings.japanese: 抱きしめたいけれど、抱きしめられない…
findings.todokanai: She wants to hold me tight, but she can't bring herself to…
